items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: It’s like when Eisenhower was talking to Nikita Khrushchev, you know the New York Times printed a whole transcript of that on two pages

ctx.x: Isn’t it ironic or I’m not sure what the word is, that you had a whole nation going to war over that issue and we still have a problem. And maybe as you said there’s a simpler way to deal with it than we have been.

Well if you listen to those people, they always invoke God. And that’s because they don’t believe in God. The people who believe in God you never hear them say His name. It’s the ones who have no belief in any God that are always talking about — as God as my judge. It’s like when Eisenhower was talking to Nikita Khrushchev, you know the New York Times printed a whole transcript of that on two pages, two full pages of the New York Times. And I always read the Times for that reason. If I want to know what someone…

you didn’t spy on us and we shot down your U-2, we have your Francis Gary Powers. And Eisenhower said well don’t tell me that you people don’t spy on us. And Khrushchev said as God is my judge, we have sent no planes over your territory. He says we know who you are and we know how much you dislike us. We don’t have to spy on you to find out about it. And Eisenhower says well it’s funny you should speak of God, when everybody knows you’re atheist. And Khrushchev says we are not atheistic. We just don’t believe in…

items.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: when MacArthur and Eisenhower fired on the people who came to get relief from the unemployment.

ctx.x: So he was a full-time minister?

Oh yes. Yes, except during the Depression he had to work as a barber in order to eat, because times were tough during the Depression. There are a lot of jokes about that, but they were. It was incredible. It was – if I hadn’t lived through it, I don’t think I would have believed it. That was really a bad time. There was the march on Washington of the unemployed, which is now being shown on television, when MacArthur and Eisenhower fired on the people who came to get relief from the unemployment. A very dark…
So your dad was a pretty important figure in your life.
